messages:
Mike S.: @acme-dev escalated — their requests are routing to us-east and causing ~200ms extra latency from EU customers. They claim they send X-Client-Region: eu-west. Can someone take a quick look? :eyes:
Julia R.: can you drop a sample curl + raw headers from the client? also which SDK/version?
acme-dev: here's literally what our infra sets (we only control header value):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: euwest' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat' 
```
(weirdly we only saw this after upgrading an internal proxy that adds a null terminator to header values)
Mike S.: ahhh — null byte in header. That will likely fail strict token match and fall back to default region. logs attached from our edge showing region token after parsing: `region_token=\u0000eu-west` then router normalized it to blank and used default us-east.
Ingrid L.: runtime note — we have a recent change in the header sanitizer that rejects non-printable/control chars by stripping them then doing a strict lookup. If stripping leaves an empty string we call the fallback path (default-region). That explains the behavior.
runtime-bot: DETECTED: 17 requests in last 5m from acme-dev with invalid region token (contains control char). Routing fallback to default-region triggered.
Julia R.: repro steps for support: 1) run the curl above (note the \u0000 in header) 2) look at request.trace id in our edge logs 3) confirm `router.region` = default-region in logs.
Mike S.: proposed customer workaround: ensure client sanitizes header (strip \u0000) or send region via query param `?region=eu-west` for now. Also advise pinning SDK to prev proxy behavior.
Ingrid L.: long-term fix: 1) change router normalization to unicode-normalize + remove control chars but NOT silently produce empty — instead treat as invalid and surface 400 with error `invalid_region_header` when explicit region header present. 2) add metric for `invalid_region_header` and log the raw header for diagnostics (one-way hashed). 3) ship patch to canary tomorrow (runtime v1.2.3-canary).
Mike S.: I'll notify the customer about workaround + ETA. Created internal ticket SUP-1987, assigned to @Ingrid L. Patch PR: https://git.redwood/sup/PR-4512  (canary scheduled). :thumbsup:
Julia R.: adding support note to include exact copy/paste example showing how to strip nulls: 
```
# node example
const val = receivedHeader.replace(/\u0000/g, '').trim();
```
acme-dev: thanks — we'll roll that fix out and confirm after your canary. Appreciate the quick triage!
Mike S.: marking resolved on our side once canary is in and customer verifies. Will follow up in this thread with canary results.
